name: Urea reactor
description: High-pressure reactor in which ammonia and carbon dioxide form ammonium carbamate and then dehydrate to urea. Conversion per pass is incomplete, so the high-pressure loop strips and recycles unconverted carbamate; reactor pressure, temperature and the ammonia-to-CO2 ratio set conversion and downstream stripping duty. Primary source: https://www.saipem.com/sites/default/files/2019-03/spm_UREAri_L02_14_01_10.pdf
applications: urea synthesis in nitrogen fertiliser plants

specifications.basis: Snamprogetti process; patents quote 2.5-3.5 with 3.0-3.2 preferred
share of CO2 entering the reactor converted to urea; the high-pressure loop reaches 85-90% overall
2 NH3 + CO2 <-> NH4CO2NH2 at 110 atm and 160 C; fast exothermic
NH4CO2NH2 <-> CO(NH2)2 + H2O, slow endothermic, at 160-180 C
worldwide production capacity in 2020, cited to IFASTAT
2 urea -> biuret + NH3; suppressed in synthesis reactor by maintaining excess ammonia
ammonium carbamate highly corrosive even to resistant stainless; passive oxide layer maintained by oxygen injection
specifications.value: continuous small oxygen (air) injection; duplex stainless (1990s); zirconium or zirconium-clad titanium tubing (2000s)

specifications.basis: SensoTech application note: thermal conversion of ammonium carbamate at a temperature of 200 C and pressure 130 to 200 bar

sources.note: Saipem urea technology brochure (pressure, temperature, N/C ratio, conversion), read 2026-11-17

notes: The Saipem numbers describe its NH3-stripping flowsheet; CO2-stripping licensors run comparable HP-loop conditions (about 140 bar and 185-190 °C in the patents read) but the figures are not interchangeable. Enriched 2026-11-24 with page-read ammonia/urea sweep sources. Enriched 2026-11-24 with page-read ammonia/urea sweep sources.
